title: Introduce credit-gated flush and microloop shedder to reduce streaming tail latency
author: Maya Kim
description: Motivation: several customer canaries and internal traces showed sporadic streaming tail spikes caused by an interaction between the emission microloop, conservative flush cadence, and indiscriminate token credits that allowed long-running streams to block microbatches. This PR introduces a credit-gated flush controller and a microloop shedder that cooperatively: (1) decouples the emission loop from flush timing so short-lived streams can flush quickly without waiting for global flush ticks, (2) enforces per-stream soft credit budgets to prevent noisy long streams from starving kernel coalescing, and (3) speculatively presizes KV cache windows for fast warm-up when a stream is prioritized. The design is opt-in via feature flag stream.flush_gating_enabled and includes an adaptive heuristic that lowers per-stream credit when we detect kernel contention or low host GPU utilization. Implementation summary: added a light-weight credit allocator in emitter/core, replaced the monolithic flush timer with a gated flush controller, introduced a microloop shedder that yields CPU between heavy emitters, and wired a speculative_kv_presize hint into kv/cache_manager. Safety: preserves backward compatibility by defaulting feature flag to off; canary rollout instructions included. Observability: new metrics stream_credit_consumed, stream_shed_count, gated_flush_latency_p50/p95 and traces annotated with gate decisions. Results: internal canary on dedicated cluster (r5-redwood-gtx) shows 95th percentile TTFB reduction of ~18% on mixed chat workloads and stable throughput with no regression in token-per-second efficiency. See linked benchmarks in the PR for workload breakdowns.

review_conversation:
Ava Patel: Can you walk through the safety properties if speculative_kv_presize overshoots and causes extra memory pressure?
Maya Kim: We cap presize at a conservative per-host limit and the cache_manager signals backpressure; tests included to validate host OOM scenarios.
Diego Martinez: I saw a flaky test in the first CI run (streaming_integration.LegacyFlushTick). What caused it?
Maya Kim: The initial refactor left the legacy timer active in a race with gated controller. I pushed a follow-up commit that ensures the legacy timer is disabled when the flag is set; CI now passes.
Lena Chu: Did you try lowering credits automatically under sustained kernel contention?
Maya Kim: Yes — the allocator monitors kernel queue length and will halve per-stream credits when avg_queue_depth > threshold for N windows. Open to tuning the thresholds.
Ava Patel: Looks good; please add a short note in docs that this is opt-in for private deployments because presize hints are memory-sensitive.
Maya Kim: Added docs and the canary pipeline; responding to all comments and added more unit coverage.
Review outcome: approved by Ava and Lena, Diego gave +1 after flake fix. The PR was squashed and merged.
release_notes: Introduce credit-gated flush controller and microloop shedder to reduce streaming tail latency. Opt-in via feature flag stream.flush_gating_enabled. Adds metrics for gated flush decisions and KV presize hints. Backwards compatible by default.
